nodes.label: ADR 0002 - Game content and balance in shared JSON
nodes.community_name: Non-negotiable rules (English, no balance numbers in code, pure engine, pinned deps)
nodes.norm_label: adr 0002 - game content and balance in shared json
nodes.rationale: Duplicated per-language constants diverge silently; shared/data/*.json validated by JSON Schema makes new content a data change (Open/Closed). Go needs a go generate copy step since go:embed cannot read parent dirs.

nodes.label: ADR 0003 - Deterministic pure engine with shared PRNG and golden tests
nodes.community_name: Non-negotiable rules (English, no balance numbers in code, pure engine, pinned deps)
nodes.norm_label: adr 0003 - deterministic pure engine with shared prng and golden tests
nodes.rationale: Parity must be verifiable; language RNGs and float math differ, so the engine is a pure step(command)->events state machine with mulberry32 and integer floor math; Python generates golden files that ports replay.

nodes.label: ADR 0004 - Full-screen TUI with Textual, Ink and Bubble Tea
nodes.community_name: Non-negotiable rules (English, no balance numbers in code, pure engine, pinned deps)
nodes.norm_label: adr 0004 - full-screen tui with textual, ink and bubble tea
nodes.rationale: Animated art, live bars and combat log need full-screen TUI; use each ecosystem's most popular framework with layout specified once in docs/tui.md (100x30); differing paradigms are didactic. Later ports use ratatui, FTXUI and a hand-written ANSI renderer for Elixir.

nodes.label: ADR 0005 - Python built first as the reference
nodes.community_name: Non-negotiable rules (English, no balance numbers in code, pure engine, pinned deps)
nodes.norm_label: adr 0005 - python built first as the reference
nodes.rationale: Designing in several languages at once multiplies design churn; Python delivers the full game first, ports are mechanical and test-driven via golden files; Python is the tie-breaker when docs are ambiguous.

nodes.label: Battle Turn Order of Operations
nodes.rationale: Random numbers are consumed in exactly the written order so all ports produce identical events.

nodes.label: Game Loop (Title -> Merchant <-> Battle -> Game Over)
nodes.norm_label: game loop (title -> merchant <-> battle -> game over)

nodes.label: Infinite Tier Progression and Cycle Scaling (NG+)
nodes.norm_label: infinite tier progression and cycle scaling (ng+)

nodes.label: Engine Event Catalog (flat camelCase JSON events)
nodes.norm_label: engine event catalog (flat camelcase json events)

nodes.label: Bubble Tea v2 + Lip Gloss TUI
nodes.norm_label: bubble tea v2 + lip gloss tui

nodes.label: Menus as Data (Action enum)
nodes.rationale: Closures capturing &mut self fight the borrow checker.

nodes.label: Event/Command Enums with serde Internally Tagged Representation
nodes.norm_label: event/command enums with serde internally tagged representation
nodes.rationale: Missing or misspelled fields become compile errors and exhaustive match forces consumers to be revisited.

nodes.label: Framework-Independent UI Controller (press(key))
nodes.rationale: Porting the UI = porting the controller (unit-testable without a terminal) + a thin renderer.

nodes.label: Run Statistics, Profile and Achievements
nodes.rationale: Achievements and timestamps are outside the deterministic engine; computed by the application layer from events.

nodes.label: save.json (single active run, rngState snapshot)
nodes.rationale: Loading restores RunState and PRNG so a continued run is identical to an uninterrupted one; written atomically via tmp + rename.

nodes.label: Observer-like Event Stream
nodes.rationale: One event stream feeds statistics, bestiary, achievements and the UI.

nodes.label: schemaVersion and Migrations
nodes.rationale: Newer files are never overwritten; older ones are migrated; format change = MINOR if migrations keep old files readable, MAJOR otherwise.

nodes.label: Explicit to_dict/from_dict Serialisation (no pickle)
nodes.rationale: The save format is shared with the other five implementations.

nodes.label: Golden Tests (shared/golden replay)
nodes.rationale: Golden files are generated only by the Python reference and only regenerated with an intended rule change.

nodes.label: Balance Targets and Simulator (greedy bot)
nodes.rationale: The bot is a floor, not a ceiling; re-run the simulator after any balance change.

nodes.label: Endless Roguelite Direction (Tibia-inspired)
nodes.rationale: Turns two small learning projects (Python 2016, TypeScript 2022) into one didactic open-source monorepo with the same game in several languages.

nodes.label: Four Test Levels (unit, integration, golden, e2e)
nodes.norm_label: four test levels (unit, integration, golden, e2e)

nodes.label: GameEngine.step(command) -> events (state machine + command/event)
nodes.rationale: The TUI never mutates state; it sends commands and renders events, making the core testable without a terminal and enabling golden tests and the simulator.

nodes.label: Not Doing List (multiplayer, sound, extra locales, sprites, meta-progression)
nodes.norm_label: not doing list (multiplayer, sound, extra locales, sprites, meta-progression)

nodes.label: Clean Architecture Layers (domain/application/infrastructure/presentation)
nodes.rationale: Dependencies point inwards only; the domain knows nothing about files, terminals, clocks or JSON, so rules are testable and portable across six languages.

nodes.label: Data-Driven Content (Open/Closed)
nodes.rationale: New monsters, items or spells are JSON edits, not code changes.

nodes.label: Repository Pattern + Ports
nodes.rationale: Ports keep domain/application free of I/O.
